items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8484

SPONSOR: COONEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to establishing the
Charles L. Reason fellowship for the purpose of increasing faculty
diversity in higher education in New York

 
PURPOSE:

Establishes the Charles L. Reason fellowship in higher education

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 article 130 of title 7 of the education law is renumbered
article 129-C and a new section 6457 is added which sets forth the
requirements for the Charles L. Reason fellowship

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Over the past five years, data trends in postsecondary education show a
significant distinct imbalance between student and faculty diversity.
According to the Pew Research Center, college students in the United
States are twice as likely as academic faculty members to be black, and
four times as likely to be Hispanic. The same study reported more than
75 percent of college faculty members in the United States are white,
compared to approximately 50 percent of postsecondary students. These
and other demographic (racial, ethnic, and gender) gaps exist across
various academic disciplines in higher education, with notable under
representation in a variety of fields such as STEM, education, and
liberal arts.

The Charles L. Reason Fellowship would provide a pathway for students
with financial need who have demonstrated strong academic potential to
succeed in doctoral studies and pursue careers in academia.  Studies
show that the retention, graduation, and post baccalaureate enrollment
rates for students who participate in early exposure programs are
substantially higher than those of the general student population. This
initiative will take necessary steps toward reducing the serious under
representation of faculty members from minority groups, and toward
addressing the consequences of racial disparities in the higher educa-
tion system itself and for the larger society that it serves.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Proposed annual budget line-item appropriation of $10 million

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
